Ankudinoff’s veffel was wrecked, and the crew ditributed among the other two. Soon after this the two veffels loft light of each other, and never joined again. Delhoff was driven about by tempelluous winds till October, when he was flipwrecked confidarably to the fourth of the Andyr. Having at last reached that river, he formed a scheme of returning by the fame way that he had come, but never made the attempt. As for Alexeeff, after being alfo hipwrecked, he had died of the furry, together with Ankudinoff; part of the crew were killed by the favages, and a few escaped to Kamfchatka, where they fettled." From Captain Cook's voyage towards the northeaftern parts of Afia, it appears that it is polible to double the promontory of Tichutki without any great difficulty: and it now appears, that the continents of Afia and America are feparated from one another but by a narrow fitrait, which is free from ice; but, to tl northwards, that experienced navigator was everywhere topped by the ice in the month of August, fo that I could neither trace the American continent farther th to the latitude of 70°, nor reach the mouth of the riv Kovyma on the Afiatic continent; though it is pr bable that this might have been done at another tim., when the situation of the ice was altered either by winds or currents. On the whole, therefore, it appears that the infurmountable obtacle in the north-east pallage lies between the rivers Pialida and Chatanga; and unlefs there be in that space a connection between the Afiatic and Amerrican continents, there is not in any other part. however, is as effectual an obstruction as land : though the voyage were to be made by accident once, it never could be efteemed a paffage calcul for the purposes of trade, or any other beneficial pole whatever. With regard to the north-weft pallage, the fame ... ficulties occur as in the other. Captain Cook's voyage has now affured us, that if there is any fitait which divides the continent of America into two, it muit lie in a higher latitude than 70°, and consequently be perpetually frozen up. If a north-weft pallage can be found then, it muit be by failing round the whole American continent, instead of feeking a pallage through it, which fome have supposed to exit at the bottom of Baffin's bay. But the extent of the American continent to the northward is yet unknown; and there is a profilibility of its being joined to that part of Afia between the Pialida and Chatanga, which has never yet been
</britannica>

Wikipedia article "Geographical pole", passages:
<wikipedia>
[1] A geographical pole or geographic pole is either of the two points on Earth where its axis of rotation intersects its surface. The North Pole lies in the Arctic Ocean while the South Pole is in Antarctica. North and South poles are also defined for other planets or satellites in the Solar System, with a North pole being on the same side of the invariable plane as Earth's North pole. Relative to Earth's surface, the geographic poles move by a few metres over periods of a few years. This is a combination of Chandler wobble, a free oscillation with a period of about 433 days; an annual motion responding to seasonal movements of air and water masses; and an irregular drift towards the 80th west meridian. As cartography and geodesy require exact and unchanging coordinates, the average or nominal locations of geographical poles are taken as fixed cartographic poles or geodetic poles, the points where the body's great circles of longitude intersect; in practice this is achieved by keeping latitude values of survey markers fixed and accounting for time variations in terms of Earth orientation parameters.
</wikipedia>
